title: Apply the laws of logarithms
text: Before we can apply the law of logarithms for turning a difference into a quotient, we must handle the coefficient $$\frac{1}{2}$$. One way to handle this is to use the law of logarithms for powers: \n $$c\log_b(a)=\log_b(a**c)$$

title: Apply the laws of logarithms
text: Next apply the law of logarithms for quotients: $$\log_b(a)-\log_b(c)=\log_b(a/c).$$ \n $$\log_5(x-1)-\log_5\left((x+1)**{1/2}\right)=\log_5\left(\frac{x-1}{(x+1)**{1/2}}\right)=0$$

title: The input is $$1$$.
text: If $$\log_5\left(\frac{x-1}{(x+1)**{1/2}}\right)=0,$$ this means that the input $$\frac{x-1}{(x+1)**{1/2}}=1.$$ Now we must solve this algebraic problem.

title: Square both sides
text: Let's get rid of the fractional exponent by squaring both sides. Then apply $$\left(a**{1/2}\right)**2=a$$ and $$\frac{b**a}{c**a}=(b/c)**a$$ \n $$\left(\frac{x-1}{(x+1)**{1/2}}\right)**2=1**2$$ \n $$\frac{(x-1)**2}{(x+1)}=1$$

title: Clear the denominator
text:
This step might seem counterintuitive, but to solve for $$x, $$ it will be helpful to clear the denominator by multiplying both sides by $$(x+1).$$ 

$$\left( rac{(x-1)**2}{(x+1)}ight)\cdot{(x+1)}=1\cdot{(x+1)}$$ 

$$\left(x-1ight)^2=x+1$$

title: Interpret solutions based on domain
text: The two solutions are $$x=0$$ and $$x=3$$. However, the solution $$x=0$$ does not make sense because it would make the input of $$\log_5(x-1)$$ negative. So the only solution in the domain is $$x=3$$.
